item.title: Egypt's top security body agrees to help Saudi Arabia defend itself against Houthi attacks
item.description:
Egypt pledged “all necessary and possible forms of support ” to Saudi Arabia as intensifying Houthi attacks risk a widening regional conflict. Following the announcement, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi requested an urgent parliamentary session to authorize military action, bringing the Arab world’s largest army a step closer to direct involvement and marking a shift in Cairo’s posture. Egypt stopped short of joining a mutual defense agreement between Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, and Pakistan, but is losing billions annually from Houthi strikes. Cairo’s pledge also signals closer alignment with Riyadh, a major financial backer that has provided billions in aid and investment. “Cairo, whether it likes it or not, has become a party to the war ,” a Saudi columnist wrote in Asharq Al-Awsat. — Lauren Morganbesser

item.title: Macron condemns violence after riots lead to looting and mass arrests
item.description:
Paris woke Sunday to shattered storefronts, burned cars and a heavy police presence after unrest swept through the city and other parts of France. Violent clashes broke out Saturday during nationwide demonstrations over rising living costs and poor school conditions. Hundreds of thousands marched across the country, while masked groups fought with police, looted businesses and set fires in several cities. Police reported 1,800 arrests nationwide, including 855 in the Paris region. VIOLENCE ERUPTS AT FRANCE PROTESTS AS MACRON WARNS UNREST IS BEING EXPLOITED The destruction was not limited to Paris. In Limoges, about three hours south of the capital, fire tore through the city’s historic town hall, built in 1883 and designated a historic landmark in 1975. item.title: 'No Kings' protesters rally across the US – video
item.description:
Protesters held rallies across the US as part of the 'No Kings' movement, voicing opposition to the Trump administration and calling for early voting ahead of November's midterm elections. The rallies coincide with heightened legal battles surrounding voting rules, including a recent federal lawsuit filed against California regarding mail-in ballots and warnings from the justice department concerning ballot processing. item.title: Meloni backs police after cost-of-living protests turn violent in Italian cities
item.description:
Hundreds at Lisbon tent camp demand action, as Giorgia Meloni says march in Italy was exploited by ‘hooligans’ The angry protests that have convulsed Spain and France in recent weeks have spilled over to Italy and Portugal, with rioters clashing with police and setting property on fire in Milan, and a tent encampment springing up in Lisbon over the weekend. A march in central Milan on Saturday to protest against rising living costs began peacefully but ended with masked rioters throwing stones, paving blocks and other objects at riot police and setting fire to barricades made from bar tables.
